title: findings@6
description: The JUDGE-BOUNDARY document, successor to findings@2 (refit of 2026-08-21). Declared on review fanout steps, review-security, and design-qa ONLY — never on reconcile: the builtin `aggregate` carries through only the input element's own keys, so a schema requiring `id` on the aggregate document makes the §7.6 E5 conjunction unsatisfiable and V30 refuses the workflow at register time (findings@5 remains the reconcile document for exactly that reason). findings@2 was orphaned when the DOT-483 nullable-line fix repointed every judge step to findings@5, the cluster document requiring only `severity` — a silent downgrade that dropped the per-judge refusal of malformed payloads built after RUN-5 recorded findings keyed `location`/`rule` that everything downstream silently dropped. This version restores findings@2's boundary and folds in what was learned since: `line` widens to integer-or-null (DOT-483 — a whole-file or whole-commit finding has no single line), and `prior_disposition` is declared because judges legitimately set it on re-review rounds (observed on judge-security in RUN-35). Under this document a malformed judge payload refuses at that judge's own `complete`, with per-judge attribution, instead of vanishing later.

id.description: Stable identifier for the finding, unique within the payload. Required here, unlike the cluster documents: this document is never declared on the aggregate step, so the V30 concern that keeps `id` optional there does not apply.

severity.description: The finding's severity, on 02 §6's five-value ladder. The enum's document order IS the order thresholds compare on (`any(severity >= high)`): info < low < medium < high < blocker. Judges author on the general or security ladder fragment and map onto these values at emit time.

file.description: Repo-relative path the finding is anchored to. Required: an unanchored finding cannot be clustered by locus or acted on by fix.

line.description: 1-indexed line within `file`. Optional per 02 §6. An explicit `null` is ALSO valid — a finding whose scope is the whole file or the whole commit has no single line to anchor to (DOT-483); that is distinct from simply omitting the key. `minimum` applies only when the value is a number, so the integer case stays constrained and null passes untouched.

evidence.description: What a skeptic can re-run or re-read to confirm the finding.

alternative.description: A concrete alternative to the flagged approach. Optional at every severity (see findings@1's note on DKT-51).

prior_disposition.description: How this same locus was already ruled on in an EARLIER fix-loop round. On a judge document this is rare and legitimate: a re-review judge whose inputs carry an earlier ruling on a locus it is re-examining may annotate the re-occurrence rather than present settled ground as a discovery. Sub-fields per findings@5's declaration; every one optional so a partially-known disposition is still recordable.

round.description: The fix-loop round the ruling was made in, 0-based — round 0 is the first review, before any fix step ran.

ruling.description: What was decided, in the decider's terms. Conventional forms: `accepted`, `corrected-to-<severity>`, `rejected`, or `deferred` (which `follow_up_issue` must then name).

ruled_by.description: Who decided: `operator`, or `panel <proposal-id>` where a tribunal did.

follow_up_issue.description: The issue id the deferred work was filed as.
